ti: Broaden PS1001 — it misses per-element AtF64/SetF64 outside Numel/Unravel loops
PS3003 is blind to named integer map keys — it cannot see any enum-keyed dispatch table
Triage the 22 PS4004 findings and tighten the rule if the false-positive rate warrants it

note:
FIXED. PS3003 now reports the canonical case it always should have caught.

THREE CAUSES, all closed:
(1) integerKeyType rejected a *ast.SelectorExpr key (backend.Op) on its first line and a non-builtin *ast.Ident (Op) one line later. Fixed with a repo-scoped registry of named integer types harvested from the scanned source in a pre-pass — the go/types approach originally specified was INFEASIBLE, since perfscan is AST-only (go/ast, go/parser, no packages.Load) and adding package loading would have changed the tool architecture.
(2) intKeyMapNames ValueSpec arm never inspected x.Values, so a package-level var m = map[K]V{} with the type on the composite literal registered as nothing.
(3) THE STRUCTURAL ONE, and the reason the first two were not enough: intKeyMapNames is FILE-SCOPED, while a dispatch registry is declared in one file and read in another (vjps at autograd/vjp.go:19, hot read at autograd/autograd.go:176). Package-level map vars are now collected into a per-package registry in a pre-pass and merged into each file set — package-level declarations ONLY, since hoisting function-local maps package-wide would let a name in one file mark an unrelated same-named local in another.

RESULT: autograd.go now reports vjps. Tree-wide findings 4 -> 33, fixture suite unchanged and green, gofmt and vet clean. Committed as afd1aa8 (and 591f81b for causes 1 and 2).

PUZZLE RESOLVED rather than left open: the intermediate 4 -> 32 jump was entirely plain integer-keyed LOCAL maps with zero enum-keyed ones, which I had flagged as unexplained. Cause (3) explains it — every enum-keyed registry in this repo is declared apart from its read, so none could ever appear. The silent reproduction and the missing enum findings were one bug seen from two sides.

STILL OUTSTANDING: the 29 findings beyond the original 4 are UNTRIAGED. Classify each as a real map-to-slice candidate or a false positive to be excluded by construction, and state the verdict per site. Most are plain int-keyed locals and probably genuine, but that is an expectation, not a verdict.

SEPARATE, OPTIONAL, do not bundle: converting vjps/vjpsMulti to [backend.NumOps]VJP arrays saves roughly 8-12 ns per node, about 20 us on a 2000-node backward — 1-2 percent, honestly small. Bit-identical, needs its own benchmark.

METHOD, earned the hard way across four attempts on this one rule: an isolated cause can be real, necessary, and still not sufficient. Three reasoned fixes each left the site silent; a single instrumented print of the call site located the truth in one run. Instrument the reproduction before patching, and check what a metric actually counts before attributing it.

txt: WHEN a new check is added, the perfscan check registry SHALL its ID MUST be verified free on main AND in every open PR that touches the registry — grep the candidate ID out of `gh pr diff <n>` for each open PR before minting it.
WHEN a new check ID is minted, the perfscan check registry SHALL reject any ID not verified free on main and in every open PR touching the registry, via `gh pr diff` per PR.

WHEN a //perfscan:ignore directive is written, the a perfscan suppression SHALL re-run the scan and confirm the finding is gone; a directive that fails to apply is silently inert and reads as accepted.

body:
Closing this line of work with a full diagnosis so a fourth attempt does not repeat the first three.

THE CLASS is the highest-value one this campaign found: work rebuilt once per iteration of an enclosing loop when it depends on nothing that loop produces. Removing it deletes a FACTOR, not a constant — the measured instance took an SVD backward term from O(m n^3) to O(m n^2), -96.5 percent, with the ratio growing with n exactly as a factor predicts.

ATTEMPT 1 (withheld): report an inner loop nest whose body never mentions the IMMEDIATE enclosing index. Found 0 on its own motivating site and 2 on the FIXED site, 106 tree-wide. Wrong in both directions: the motivating nest is invariant in a GRANDPARENT while genuinely depending on its parent, and a correctly hoisted nest legitimately does not mention the outer index either.

ATTEMPT 2 (withheld): test invariance against EVERY enclosing index, and treat locals the enclosing loop assigns as carriers of its index — which correctly suppresses already-hoisted code, since a hoisted nest reads locals like ui := u[i]. Still 0 on the motivating site, and it exempted names the nest itself writes, which was unsound: that exemption reported a QR solve whose reflector loop consumes a per-column vector the enclosing loop fills.

ATTEMPT 3 (withheld): attempt 2 with the unsound exemption removed. Sound, and finds NOTHING — 0 sites tree-wide.

THE DIAGNOSIS: the motivating transform is not loop hoisting at all, it is loop DISTRIBUTION. The invariant work was a PREFIX of statements inside a loop whose remaining statements depend on the index; the fix splits the loop body into an invariant part and a dependent part and lifts the first. No loop-level predicate can see that, because the loop as a whole IS dependent. Catching it needs statement-level dependence analysis inside a body, plus scope promotion for anything the lifted prefix writes.

RECOMMENDATION: do not attempt this again as an AST predicate without that analysis. The measured instance is recorded in the T1051 commit and remains the evidence that the class is worth a real implementation if one is ever built.

txt: WHEN a new check looks for unused parallelism, the its author SHALL run it tree-wide and classify EVERY candidate before shipping, because the shapes an applied conversion leaves behind look exactly like the shape being hunted.

IF PS3059 reports one nest in a function, THEN the reader SHALL read the whole function anyway, because the check has been observed to report the colder of two nests of its own shape and the cause is not yet isolated.

WHEN a scripted source edit asserts its anchor is unique before replacing, the author SHALL verify afterwards that the edit landed in the intended function, because a uniqueness assert on a short prelude can pass against a match elsewhere in the file.
